ApprovalPolicy.description:
A session's approval policy — what happens to an  {@link  ApprovalService }  ask BEFORE any interactive answerer sees it:

- `'ask'` (the default) — delegate to the composed answerers; with none   composed the chain falls through to the fail-closed `'unavailable'`.
- `'never'` — never prompt anyone: every ask resolves `'rejected'`   deterministically. The strict headless stance (CI, unattended runs) and   the policy whose outcome is knowable without asking.

ApprovalPolicyEventData.description: The session's approval policy was switched — log-only, durable, replayable, never in the model transcript (the model learns the policy from the runtime-context snapshot and live switch notices). The LAST such event is the session's override. `source: 'delegation'` marks an override seeded into a child; an absent source is a runtime switch.

source.description: Marks an override seeded into a child at delegation.

AssistantMessageEventData.description: Assembled assistant message for one step (derived history uses this). Carries the step's `usage` when the adapter reported token accounting, so the model output and its accounting travel together (there is no separate usage record). `usage` is absent when the adapter reported none. A turn cancelled mid-stream finalizes its delivered text/reasoning prefix as this event with `interrupted: true`; undispatched tool calls are absent. The marker distinguishes that prefix without re-deriving interruption from turn boundaries. An aborted turn with no such event streamed no visible content.

ProviderConfiguration.description: The small, portable subset of a provider profile the terminal edits.

api.description: Wire protocol the stored profile names (e.g. `openai-responses`), when it names one. Load-only: the editor never writes it, but endpoint discovery passes it so the listing speaks the same protocol as real requests.

configured.description: Whether the reference currently resolves to a stored value.

source.description: Source layer supplying the value; absent while unconfigured.

writable.description: Whether a write through this panel would currently succeed.

ProviderDiscoveryRequest.description: Model discovery against an endpoint the user is configuring.

ProviderModelSettings.description: One explicit model enabled for a provider profile.

extras.description: Remaining entry fields the editor does not model (`reasoningEfforts`, `compat`, `input`, …), carried verbatim so a save preserves them. Populated by  {@link  loadProviderSettings } ; never contains the four modelled keys.

failures.description: Non-fatal join failures (settings/directory reads), for a degradation notice.

rows.description: Provider rows: configurable-directory order first, active-unmanaged rows after.

writable.description: Whether the settings provider accepts writes (mirrors the web page's flag).

ProviderTargetView.description: One provider row in the TUI provider-management panel: the configurable directory entry joined with its settings profile and credential facts. active.description: Whether an adapter currently serves this route.

configuration.description: Endpoint and explicit model overrides visible to the provider editor.

configured.description: Whether the resolved profile exists (the whole section, or at `settingsPath`).

credential.description: Credential facts, a bounded describe error, or undefined when there is no ref to describe.

credentialRef.description: The credential reference the resolved profile names, when one does.

declared.description: The owning adapter reports this route as hand-declared (absent when it draws no distinction).

diagnostic.description: Configuration diagnostic the adapter reported for this route (catalog or profile damage): the row stays listed and repairable instead of the whole provider vanishing; absent when the route reads clean.

removable.description: Whether only the user settings layer carries the profile, so removal restores the base.

settingsNs.description: User-settings namespace whose section configures this provider; '' when unmanaged.

settingsRevision.description: Revision of the owning settings section at load (0 when no namespace resolved).

suggestedRef.description: The conventional reference a save uses for a dormant or ref-less profile.

error.description: Optional failure identity and raw user-facing detail, outside model-facing content.

PtcDispatchStartEventData.description: Payload recorded when one nested PTC mode Tool dispatch starts.

QueueMutation.description: One mutation the terminal may request for a pending next-turn inbox item.

QueueMutationOutcome.description: What one requested queue mutation did; the runner maps it to one notice.

ReasoningBlock.description: Reasoning / thinking content, distinct from visible text.

ReplayEnvelope.description: Adapter-private lossless-JSON state for replaying a successful response, carried by a terminal `finish` chunk and stored on the assembled assistant message's model source. blocks.description: Per-block adapter-private metadata, one entry per emitted block in first-seen stream order. response.description: Response-level adapter-private metadata (ids, native stop reason).

RequestContext.description: Registration-bound metadata for one resolved model route.

contextWindow.description: Maximum combined request and response context in tokens, when advertised.

model.description: Provider-owned model id the metadata belongs to.

provider.description: Registered provider route the metadata belongs to.

systemPromptUpdate.description: `'in-history'` when the route reads the latest `system` message at any position as the effective system prompt.

RequestHeaderEventData.description: Full header for the next request, appended inside its step before dispatch. It is log-only; the latest snapshot reconstructs the request header.

startsSeries.description: This request begins a distinct model-message series, independently of the header reason.

RequestHeaderReason.description: Why a `request/header` snapshot was appended: `'initial'` — the log's first header (a new conversation); `'resume'` — a loop instance's first request over a log that already has header events (process restart, fork seed); `'change'` — a later request used a different header; `'series'` — an unchanged header began an explicitly distinct message series or followed a surface replacement. ReviewBranch.description: One branch candidate for the review picker.

ReviewCommit.description: One commit candidate for the review picker.

at.description: Committer timestamp in Unix epoch milliseconds.

SandboxMode.description: File-effect policy for confined processes. `read-only` permits only required sinks such as `/dev/null`; `workspace-write` also permits the workspace and a backend-defined temp area; `danger-full-access` bypasses confinement. ScheduleRow.description: Display shape shared by the native catalog and historical schedule events.

everySeconds.description: Recurrence seconds for 'every' rows, undefined otherwise.

targetAt.description: Next due time (epoch ms); the /schedule panel derives overdue/relative labels.

SessionEndSeedEventData.description:
Separates inherited or restored history from later lifecycle-owned work. This log-only marker need not be at  {@link  Session.firstLiveSeq  } : a fork seed can already contain its tagged marker and child-owned synthetic closers before construction.

A fresh fork child owns one `{ inherited: true }` marker at its exact inherited-prefix cut, even when that prefix ends in an ancestor marker. `buildForkSeed` appends that marker before any synthetic closers; the `Session` constructor supplies it when given only the inherited prefix. The last tagged marker is the current Session's cut; untagged markers keep ordinary restore and replay lifecycle boundaries.

Only the `Session` constructor and `buildForkSeed` may create this marker. The invariant companion deliberately constrains nothing here, so a plugin appending one would silently classify every live bracket before it as seed history.

An owner of a standalone open/close bracket (`compaction/start` … `compaction/end`) reads it because seed history and live work are otherwise byte-identical: an unmatched opening marker before this event belongs to an ended lifecycle, whatever ended it. NOT a liveness signal about other writers — a concurrently live session holds its own boundary elsewhere, so tolerating concurrent writers needs a signal beyond the log.

SessionEvent.description:
One immutable entry in the session log.

A proper discriminated union over `type` (not independent `type`/`data` unions), so `switch (event.type)` narrows `event.data` without casts.

The  {@link  sourceEventSeqs  }  and  {@link  surfaceOp  }  fields are conditional: they only exist on  {@link  SurfaceEventType }  variants (`system/message`, `user/message`, `assistant/message`, `tool/result`). Non-surface events (boundary markers, attempts, errors) never carry surface metadata — the compiler enforces this at `Session.append()` call sites.

Absent means required: a reader meeting an unrecognized type without this marker MUST refuse to reconstruct the session instead of silently dropping the event, because an unrecognized required event may change how the rest of the log is interpreted. A writer sets `true` only on purely informational records whose loss cannot affect reconstruction; defaulting to required means a forgotten marker over-refuses (an inconvenience) rather than silently resuming a gutted session.

SessionEventKnown.description: The SessionEvent members the contract knows.

SessionHeader.description: Immutable validated storage metadata, kept outside the conversation event log.

agentPreset.description: Id of the agent preset this session's agent was composed from, when the deployment composes per session. Durable because the preset decides the session's tools and prompt: a resume that restored a different composition would replay history the model can no longer act on.

createdAt.description: Non-negative safe-integer Unix epoch milliseconds when the session was created.

cwd.description: Absolute working directory the session was created in (if any).

delegationDepth.description: Delegation depth: absent (zero) for a top-level session, parent depth + 1 for a subagent child. Persisted so a recursion budget survives restart and resume — a runtime-only depth would reset a resumed child to top-level.

id.description: The session's id (mirrors the  {@link  Session  } 's id).

isSeeded.description: Whether this Session contains a fork-inherited event prefix. The exact prefix length is Session state rather than ordinary header metadata.

origin.description: Coarse product classification for a session created as a subagent child. This is presentation metadata, not proof that the child is continuable.

parentSession.description: The session this one was forked from (seed lineage), if any.

version.description: Current logical format version, stamped from  {@link  SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION } . Historical physical headers are translated before entering this interface.

SessionLogDeepseekDeliveryAcceptedEventD.description: Records that the configured endpoint accepted one delivery through `throughSeq`.

sessionFormatVersion.description: Accepted Session format generation; absence identifies version 0.

sessionId.description: Session identity the accepted delivery carried; inherited fork markers retain the parent's id.

throughSeq.description: Last canonical event included in the accepted request.

SessionReferenceInput.description: One source session selected by a host.

SessionReferenceSource.description: Durable source session, cited event seqs, and snapshot facts for prepared cross-session context.

form.description: Material lifted out of another session's log (`recall` context form).

capturedFormatVersion.description: Source Session format generation; absence identifies version 0.

updatedAt.description: Last-activity timestamp: artifact mtime when known, else createdAt.

messageSeqs.description: Exact human `user/message` seqs used to derive this title; empty for an explicit user rename.

source.description: Whether the built-in fallback, a registered provider, or the user supplied the title.

SessionTitleLlmRequestEventData.description: Exact model-visible request recorded before one auxiliary title dispatch.

titleProvider.description: Registered title-provider identity responsible for the request.

SessionTitleModelIdentity.description: Exact auxiliary model route that produced a title.

kind.description: Explicit user rename: pins the title — automatic generation stops scheduling.

SessionTitleSource.description: Durable ownership record for an accepted session title.

SkillCatalogSource.description: Durable provider and item records for one published session skill catalog. The catalog is a `catalog`-form context, so it records the entries it published beside the model-facing prose: a consumer presenting the list must not re-parse the `<available_skills>` block, whose framing exists for the model.

entries.description: Exactly the entries this message published, in catalog order.

update.description: Marks a replacement catalog rather than this session's first publication.

SkillInvocationSource.description: Durable source for the context message a user-explicit skill invocation injects: the user's own words ride a plain user message, and the rendered skill body follows as injected `instructions`-form context carrying this source, so transcript consumers present the injection from metadata instead of re-parsing the model-facing text.

form.description: Injected skill bodies are instructions for the model to follow.

name.description: Invoked skill name, validated user-invocable at the injecting boundary.

StepStartEventData.description: Opens step `step` of turn `turn` — one model call plus the tool executions it requested.

replayState.description: Replay metadata for a successful response; see  {@link  ReplayEnvelope } .

StreamChunk.description: Raw streaming protocol emitted by adapters. Block indexes correlate interleaved deltas, and `block-end` carries the assembled block. Adapters emit usage before the terminal finish and nothing afterward; tool arguments remain raw JSON strings. An adapter implementation may throw, but `LlmRuntime.stream()` normalizes that failure to a terminal `error` or `aborted` finish before exposing it to consumers.

SubagentCatalogEvent.description: Parent catalog v0 records known modes; v1 also retains children with unknown mode.

SubagentDescriptorData.description: The supported durable subagent identity and optional continuation composition.

SubagentModelSelectionPolicyEventData.description: Records that this session's delegation tool exposes child provider, model, and reasoning-effort selection. Appended before the first model request; absence means the fixed-route definition. Log-only: it carries no `surfaceOp` and never enters model history.

allowedModels.description: Exact routes this Session may select explicitly for a child.

SubagentSettledMessageSource.description: Durable attribution for the runtime's own account of a continuable child settling. Deliberately a different kind from  {@link  AgentMessageSource } : an Agent message is content the sender chose, while this message is the manager stating what became of the child, and a transcript that merged them would credit the child with words it never wrote.

form.description: A runtime account shown without expanding the row (`notice` context form).

senderSessionId.description: Session id of the child that settled.

summary.description: One-line account of how the child ended.

SurfaceOp.description:
How a session event entered the ordered surface. Only valid on  {@link  SurfaceEventType }  events.

- `'append'`: added to the tail — normal path for user/assistant/tool   messages.
- `{ op: 'replace', startSeq, endSeq }`: replaces surface nodes from `startSeq`   (inclusive) through `endSeq` (inclusive) with this node. Both must exist as   surface nodes in the current surface. `startSeq === endSeq` replaces a single   node. The node's  {@link  SessionEvent.sourceEventSeqs }  must include every   shadowed surface node. Used by compaction; any surface-replacing producer   may use it.

SystemMessage.description: A rendered system prompt attributed to the system-prompt producer; empty content sends no prompt.

id.description: Stable identity preserved across every representation boundary.

source.description: Required source fields supplied by the producer.

SystemMessageEventData.description: The rendered system prompt on the model-visible surface. The loop appends the first one as surface node 0 before the step's first `user/message`. A prepared in-history route can append nonempty changes in a continuing series. An incapable route or new series normalizes text to the first system node. Normalization empties nonempty later nodes, then rewrites the head if needed, through logged per-node replacements. An empty rendering always clears all active system nodes, leaving no older instructions model-visible. Empty later nodes are dormant and project to no message; an empty head with no active later node records "no system prompt". Restored nonempty text follows the same route and series rule; empty nodes never restore older text.

SystemPromptMessageSource.description: Required source of a system-role message produced by the system-prompt plugin.

SystemPromptUpdate.description: How a model applies a system prompt that changes mid-conversation. `'in-history'`: the model reads the latest `system` message at any position of `messages` as the complete effective system prompt, so a changed prompt can follow the cached history instead of rewriting message 0.

TeamMemberEventData.description: Whole teammate lifecycle value, stored only in the Team Lead Session.

TeamMemberSnapshot.description: Whole durable value written on every teammate lifecycle change.

TeamMessageDeliveredEventData.description: Durable acknowledgement that the target Session recorded the message.

TeamMessageQueuedEventData.description: Durable mailbox enqueue, stored before delivery is attempted.

TeamMessageSnapshot.description: One peer message retained until its target Session records it.

TeamMessageSource.description: Source retained by the target Session for durable mailbox de-duplication.

TeamTaskEventData.description: Whole shared-task value, stored only in the Team Lead Session.

TeamTaskSnapshot.description: Whole durable task snapshot; every mutation increments  {@link  revision } .

TextBlock.description: Plain text visible to the end user.

TodoItem.description:
One entry in an agent's todo list — the unit of the `todo/write` whole-list snapshot declared by this package.

Deliberately minimal: a human-readable `content` line and a three-state `status`. No id, priority, or `activeForm` — the list is replaced wholesale on every write (last-write-wins), so entries need no stable identity. The three statuses describe the complete portable lifecycle needed by model and UI consumers.

content.description: What this task is — a short imperative line shown in the UI.

status.description: Lifecycle state. `in_progress` marks a task being worked now; parallel work may mark several.

TodoWriteEventData.description: Whole-list snapshot; latest write wins on replay. Log-only UI state; never derived history.

TokenUsage.description:
Token accounting for one model call (cache fields are optional).

Counts are DISJOINT: `inputTokens` is uncached input only; cached input is reported separately as `cacheReadTokens`/`cacheWriteTokens` (billed input = sum of the three). Adapters whose providers fold cache hits into a total prompt count (DeepSeek's `prompt_tokens`) subtract them out.

totalTokens.description:
Exact full-call total including aggregate prompt and output tokens.

Adapters preserve a provider total or derive it from authoritative aggregate prompt/output counters; they omit it when unavailable or inconsistent.

TokenUsageProjection.description:
Durable cumulative provider usage for a complete session log.

The four buckets are disjoint. In particular, reasoning tokens are already included in `outputTokens` and are not accumulated again.

ToolAdditionBlock.description: Activates a tool definition from the developer event's referenced request header.

tool.description: Reserved against inline definitions; the historical request header owns the schema.

toolName.description: Name of exactly one tool in the referenced historical header.

ToolCallBlock.description: A tool invocation requested by the model.

arguments.description: Raw JSON string as produced by the model.

id.description: Provider-issued call id; correlates with the matching tool result.

ToolCallEventData.description: The model requested one tool invocation: `name` with the raw `arguments` JSON string exactly as the model produced it (unparsed). `callId` pairs the call with its `tool/result`.

ToolMessageSource.description: Required source of a tool-role message carrying one tool result.

ToolRemovalBlock.description: Records the dynamic removal of a tool identified by its session-local name.

ToolRestriction.description: Per-scope filter over global tools. Restrictions intersect and do not affect scoped registrations or the reserved PTC mode transport.

allow.description: Global tool names that stay visible; everything else is removed.

deny.description: Global tool names removed from visibility.

ToolResultEventData.description: A completed tool call's model-facing result, optional internal failure identity and user-facing reason, and optional tool-private `meta` presentation payload. The reason remains outside the model-facing message. `meta` is opaque to the core (the producing tool owns its shape and reads it back in `presentResult`) but MUST be JSON-serializable: `Session.append` runtime-validates all event data with `isJsonValue`, so a non-serializable `meta` is rejected at the source, and the durable log reproduces the identical card on replay. Absent unless the tool attaches one (e.g. `dsh-tool-fs` carries its result-time contextual diff here).

error.description: Optional failure identity and raw user-facing reason, outside model content; allowed only when the message has `isError: true`.

ToolResultMessage.description: A first-class tool-role message carrying the result of one tool invocation.

id.description: Stable identity preserved across every representation boundary.

source.description: Required source fields supplied by the producer.

toolCallId.description: Provider-issued id of the tool call this message answers.

ToolSchema.description:
JSON-schema description of a tool, as sent to the model.

Declared here (not in dsh-tools) because it is part of  {@link  GenerateOptions } ; dsh-tools' ToolDefinition and dsh-system-prompt's PromptAssembly both import it from this package.

deferLoading.description: Requests deferred loading of the tool definition into model context, independently of whether a tool-addition block records the tool. Uses Anthropic's defer_loading terminology.

parameters.description: JSON Schema object for the arguments.

ToolWorkflowAgentEndData.description: Settles one previously started workflow member.

ToolWorkflowAgentStartData.description: Records one workflow member after its child Session is published.

ToolWorkflowRunEndData.description: Settles one workflow run after its live resources reach quiescence.

ToolWorkflowRunStartData.description: Opens one durable top-level workflow run record.

TurnEndCancelCause.description: Durable cancellation cause, including imports whose original coarse record carried no cause.

TurnEndEventData.description: Closes turn `turn` with the  {@link  TurnEndReason }  that ended it. A turn with no entered step has no `step/start` or `step/end`. The loop does not await a flush at turn boundaries: `dsh-session-checkpoint-policy` owns the per-request durability checkpoint, and consumers that read storage after `whenIdle()` flush themselves. Success commits the turn; rejection is reported live and does not prevent later work.

anyOf.description: A cancellation request interrupted the live turn.
The turn failed. `error` is always a structured failure: the `LlmError` facts verbatim, or `{ message: errorChain(error), code: 'UNKNOWN' }` flattened from any other error.
At least one step reached its output-token ceiling, even if a plugin continued the turn.

A crash-orphaned turn was closed after the fact: agent-loop resume appends this closer for a stored log whose last turn never ended, and session-query synthesizes it on cold reads. The loop never emits this marker live, and the events recorded before the crash remain intact.

Fork-seed construction closed a turn that was still open at the fork boundary in the source session. Only fork seeds carry this marker — the loop never emits it — and the source events before the boundary remain intact in the child.

TurnEndReason.description: The union over  {@link  TurnEndReasonMap }  — why a turn ended; plugins extend it by merging variants into the map.

TurnStartEventData.description: Opens turn `turn` before the loop claims queued input or runs pre-step. Rejection, empty input, cancellation, or failure may close it with no step; otherwise the following identified `user/message` event or batch records the messages entering the step.

TurnTokenUsage.description: Exact provider-reported token accounting for every attempt in one completed Turn.

cacheReadTokens.description: Present only when every attempt reported the bucket.

cacheWriteTokens.description: Present only when every attempt reported the bucket.

reasoningTokens.description: Output subset, present only when every attempt reported it.

routes.description: Present only when every billed attempt has provider/model attribution.

totalTokens.description: Exact aggregate prompt plus output total across all attempts.

uncachedInputTokens.description: Sum of uncached prompt input across all attempts.

TurnTokenUsageRoute.description: One provider/model route that contributed a billed request attempt.

UsageTurn.description: One completed turn's exact provider-reported accounting.

cost.description: What this turn's calls cost, or undefined when this session predates the cost ledger (the panel then shows `--` rather than inventing a price). `unknown` marks a turn whose settled calls did not all report a cost.

model.description: The model that billed this turn, or '' when nothing in the log names one. The meter's own `routes` is preferred; it is absent whenever ONE attempt went unattributed, so the turn's own assistant messages answer instead.

UsageView.description: Everything the panel reads. The totals come from the mounted projection and the per-turn rows from the meter's own fold; a missing projection renders as explicitly unavailable rather than as zeros, because an unmounted deployment and a session with no traffic are different facts.

totals.description: Provider-reported usage over the whole durable log.

UserMessage.description: A user-role specialization of the shared message representation.

id.description: Stable identity preserved across every representation boundary.

source.description: Required source fields supplied by the producer.

WorkflowAgentOutcome.description: How one `agent()` call settled: clean result, child failure (script sees `null`), or run cancellation.

WorkflowStopReason.description: Why a run settled. CLOSED union (engine-owned, consumers may exhaust): `completed` = the script ran to its final `return`; `cancelled` = the run was cancelled (caller `cancel()`/signal); `error` = the script threw, a fatal `WorkflowError` propagated, or the result failed materialization.

WorkspaceChangesEventData.description: A completed top-level turn's changed files were summarized; the summary itself stays on the Host and is served by `workspaceChanges.summary` for the event's sequence while the Session lives. The latest event for one turn replaces earlier ones.

title: DSCODE runtime operations

btw/start.description: Start a side-question child session; the client mints `childId`.

commands/execute.description: Run a slash command line; `handled` is false when no command owned it.

custom/save.description: `revision` must be the snapshot's; a stale one is refused.

host/shutdown.description: The Host exits about 50 ms after answering.

models/compactionPreview.description: Null when the session, the meter or the route's window is unknown.

models/ensureRoute.description: Prepare a provider route before switching to it; true when settings changed.

models/save.description: Persist a pick as the deployment default.

models/subagentOverride.description: Set (or with null, clear) the Host-wide model override for delegated agents.

openrouter/account.description: Account and credit facts from OpenRouter, as its module reports them.

permissions/effective.description: The session's preset, or before a session exists the pending pick or the default.

permissions/select.description: Validate a preset and apply it to the session if one exists; answers the preset.

presets/planAvailable.description: Whether the DSCODE composition offers plan mode before a session exists.

session/deliver.description: `followup` queues for the next turn (or starts one); `steer` goes into the running turn. `context` is injected ahead of the message.

session/interrupt.description: Cancel the running turn but keep and re-wake the next-turn queue.

sessions/delete.description: Delete a session subtree; the result is the message to show.

sessions/rename.description: The result is the message to show.

sessions/resolveResume.description: Resolve an id or id prefix to one root session id.

workspace/gitBranch.description: The checked-out branch, or empty when detached or not a repository.

authorization/begin.description: An interactive provider login: notices and prompts, then `done`. Prompts are answered on the uplink.

authorization/watch.description: Revision numbers; re-read `authorization/directory` when one arrives.

commands/watch.description: Slash commands for the session (or the startup set): the current value first, then each change.

models/defaults.description: The deployment default model: the current value first, then each change.

notices/watch.description: Host notices from when the stream opens.

providers/watch.description: Revision numbers; re-read `providers/directory` when one arrives.

sessions/children.description: Committed events and live assistant frames of the root's child sessions, from when the stream opens.

skills/watch.description: User-invocable skills for the session or folder: the current value first, then each change.

status/watch.description: Footer metrics, service speed and delegation board, sampled every 500 ms and sent on change.
